chapters.name: Chapter 1: The main kinds of AI tools

lessons.title: Lesson 1: A map of AI tools for small business
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Name the main kinds of AI tools and match each to a business job.
This lesson builds toward: Given the main kinds of AI tools, you will match each kind of tool to a job in your business, with one job for each of the four kinds.
You do not need dozens of apps. Most small businesses get the most from four kinds of tools.
Chat assistants (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini) write and explain: replies, descriptions, plans, checklists. Design tools (Canva and others) make flyers, social posts, menus and logos, and many now have AI features to help with text and images. Office tools (Google Docs and Sheets, Microsoft Word and Excel) hold your documents and numbers, and both companies add AI helpers to them on some plans. Tools built into other apps, like your point-of-sale, booking or email software, may also have AI features.
Start with one tool per job. Learn it well before adding another.
Words to know:
- Chat assistant: an AI tool you talk to in a chat box, such as ChatGPT, Copilot or Gemini.
- Design tool: an app for making graphics like flyers and posts, such as Canva.
- Point-of-sale (POS): the system you use to ring up sales.
Try it now: Write the four kinds of tools down the side of a page. Next to each, write one job in your business it could do this month.
You can now name the main kinds of AI tools and match each to a job in your business.

check.q: What kind of tool are ChatGPT, Copilot and Gemini?
check.why: They are chat assistants you talk with to get drafts and answers.

check.q: You want to design a new menu board. Which kind of tool would you choose?
check.why: Design tools have templates made for menus and flyers.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Getting the most from a chat assistant
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use a chat assistant to produce three different business items in one session.
This lesson builds toward: Using a free chat assistant, you will produce three different business items in one session, with your business details given once at the start and every number checked.
A chat assistant is the most flexible tool you have. It can write, rewrite, summarize, translate and plan. Open it on your phone app or at chatgpt.com, copilot.microsoft.com or gemini.google.com.
Give it your business details once at the start of a chat: "I run a two-chair barbershop in Long Beach. Our style is friendly and neighborhood. Prices: cut $30, cut and beard $40." Then ask for several things in a row: a price board, a text reminder template, a reply to a review.
Ask for options and tables when they help: "Give me three versions" or "Put this in a table." Always check the numbers it repeats back to you.
Step by step:
- Open a chat assistant.
- Give your business details once at the top.
- Ask for item 1, then item 2, then item 3.
- Ask for options or a table where it helps.
- Check every number before you use it.
Words to know:
- Summarize: to make a short version of something long.
- Template: a ready-made pattern you fill in each time.
Try it now: In one chat, give your business details, then ask for: a price board, a text reminder template with "[customer name]", and a thank-you reply to a good review.
You can now use one chat session to make several business items from your own details.

check.q: When should you give your business details in a chat session?
check.why: Giving details once at the start lets every answer in the chat use them.

check.q: The chat assistant made your price board but one price looks off. What would you do?
options: Check every number against your real prices and fix it
check.why: AI can repeat numbers wrong, so you check every one.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Making a flyer or social post with Canva
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Make a simple flyer or social media post using a free design tool.
This lesson builds toward: Using a Canva template, you will make a flyer or social media post for a real offer or event, with one main message, how to reach you, every word checked and only photos you have the right to use.
Canva is a design tool that works in a web browser and as a phone app. It has a free plan and thousands of ready-made templates for flyers, menus, social posts and business cards. Check canva.com for what the free plan includes today.
Start from a template, not a blank page. Search for what you need ("restaurant flyer", "salon Instagram post"), pick one, then change the words, colors and photos to yours. Use the text from your chat assistant.
Use your own photos or ones the tool allows you to use. Keep it simple: one main message, big readable words, your business name and how to reach you. Check the spelling of your address and phone number.
Step by step:
- Open Canva and search for a template.
- Change the words to your message.
- Swap in your photos and colors.
- Add your name, address and how to reach you.
- Check every word, then download or share.
Words to know:
- Template: a ready-made design you change to make your own.
- Free plan: the version of a tool you can use without paying, usually with some limits.
Try it now: Make a flyer or post for one real offer or event in your business using a Canva template. Check every word and save it.
You can now make a clear flyer or social post from a template with a free design tool.

check.q: What does a clear flyer have?
options: One main message and how to reach you
check.why: One main message and contact details make a flyer easy to act on.

check.q: You find a great photo online for your flyer. What would you do?
options: Use it because it is online
Crop it so no one notices
Use your own photo or one you have the right to use
check.why: You may use only photos you took or have the right to use.

chapters.name: Chapter 2: AI in your everyday office tools, and your toolkit

lessons.title: Lesson 4: AI help in documents: Google Docs and Microsoft Word
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Turn a rough note into a clean business document.
This lesson builds toward: Given rough notes and Google Docs or Microsoft Word, you will turn the notes into a clean business document with AI help, saved in your document, with legal wording checked by a professional or official source.
Most businesses keep price lists, policies and letters in Google Docs or Microsoft Word. Both are free to use in a web browser with a Google or Microsoft account. Google and Microsoft add AI helpers (Gemini and Copilot) inside them on some plans; what you see depends on your account.
If your document app has an AI helper, you can ask it to draft or rewrite right on the page. If not, draft in a chat assistant and paste the text in. Either way, the document is where you keep the final, checked version.
Good document jobs: a cancellation policy, a staff opening checklist, a price list, a letter to your landlord. For policies and anything legal, have a professional or the official source check it.
Step by step:
- Write rough notes of what you want.
- Ask an AI helper (in the document or a chat assistant) to turn them into a clean document.
- Paste or keep it in Docs or Word.
- Check facts and fix the wording.
- Save it with a clear name.
Words to know:
- Google Docs: Google's free word processor in a web browser.
- Microsoft Word: Microsoft's word processor, free on the web with a Microsoft account.
- Policy: a written rule for your business, like how cancellations work.
Try it now: Write five rough lines about your cancellation or late policy. Use AI to turn them into a clear, polite policy and save it in Docs or Word.
You can now turn rough notes into a clean business document using AI and an office tool.

check.q: Where should the final, checked version of a business policy live?
options: In your document in Docs or Word
check.why: Your document keeps the checked version safe and easy to share.

check.q: AI turned your notes into a refund policy that uses legal words. What would you do?
options: Ask AI if it is legal
Have a professional or the official source check the wording
check.why: Legal wording should be checked by a professional or official source.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: AI help in spreadsheets: Sheets and Excel
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Build a simple sales or inventory table and get AI help reading it.
This lesson builds toward: Using Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel, you will build a sales or inventory table and get AI help reading it, with at least 10 rows, a SUM formula for the total and AI's answer confirmed in the sheet.
A spreadsheet is a grid of rows and columns for numbers. Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel are the common choices. A simple table, like Date, Item, Quantity, Price, Total, already tells you a lot.
AI can help in two ways. It can tell you how to do something ("How do I total column E in Google Sheets?"), and on some plans it can work inside the sheet. You can also paste a small table with no private details into a chat assistant and ask, "Which item sold best?"
Check the math. AI is better at explaining than calculating, so let the spreadsheet do the totals with a SUM formula, and use AI to explain or suggest what to look at.
Step by step:
- Make columns: Date, Item, Quantity, Price, Total.
- Enter one week of sales.
- Ask AI how to add a SUM total, and do it.
- Ask AI which item sold best, then confirm in the sheet.
Words to know:
- Spreadsheet: a grid of rows and columns for numbers, like Google Sheets or Excel.
- Formula: an instruction in a cell that calculates, like =SUM(E2:E20).
Try it now: Make a sales or inventory table with at least 10 rows. Use a SUM formula for the total, and ask AI which item sold best. Confirm the answer in your sheet.
You can now build a simple sales table and use AI to help you read it, while the spreadsheet does the math.

options: A formula that adds up a column
check.why: SUM is a spreadsheet formula that adds numbers.

check.q: AI says your best-selling item last month was coffee. What would you do?
options: Ask AI again until it agrees
check.why: You confirm AI's reading of your data in the sheet itself.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Building your starter AI toolkit
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Choose three to five tools, assign each a job, and set a safety rule for each.
This lesson builds toward: Given the tools you tried, you will create a starter toolkit table of three to five tools with a job and a safety rule for each, listing tool, job, plan and safety rule, with free plans used before paying.
Your toolkit is a short list: the tool, its job, which plan, and a rule. For example: ChatGPT (free) for replies and descriptions; Canva (free) for flyers; Google Sheets for weekly sales; Google Docs for policies.
Before paying for any upgrade, use the free plan for a month and write down what you could not do. Pay only for a feature you truly need, and check the price on the official site.
Safety rules travel with every tool: no customer card numbers, passwords or private details; check every fact before customers see it; use only photos and words you have the right to use.
Step by step:
- List three to five tools.
- Write one job for each.
- Write "free" or the plan you pay for.
- Write one safety rule for each.
- Make one real item with each tool.
Words to know:
- Toolkit: the short list of tools you use and what each is for.
- Upgrade: a paid plan with more features.
Try it now: Final task: make your toolkit table, then make one real item with each tool: a customer message, a flyer or post, and a price list or sales table.
You can now choose, organize and safely use a small set of AI tools for your business.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Toolkit table Fewer than three tools, or a missing job, plan or safety rule. Three to five tools, each with a job, plan and safety rule. Notes when the owner would consider paying for an upgrade. Customer message No message, or it has a real customer's details or wrong facts. A checked customer message made with the chat assistant, using placeholders. The owner compared more than one version and chose the best. Flyer or post No flyer, or it has errors or photos without rights. A flyer or post with one main message and contact details, every word checked. Uses the owner's own photos and is ready to post or print. Price list or sales table No table, or totals typed by hand. A price list in Docs or Word, or a sales table with a SUM formula. AI's reading of the table was confirmed in the sheet. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: What does your toolkit table list?
options: Tool, job, plan and safety rule
check.why: Each row says which tool, its job, its plan and its safety rule.

check.q: A tool offers a paid upgrade. When would you pay for it?
options: When you need a feature the free plan lacks
check.why: Pay only when the free plan is missing something you really need.
